concept.name: A-trade
concept.definition: In the setup-grading taxonomy used in proprietary trading (popularized by Mike Bellafiore's SMB framework), the highest grade of opportunity: a trade matching the trader's best playbook patterns under favorable conditions, warranting full planned position size. The grade is a sizing decision based on the pattern class's tracked expectancy, not a claim about certainty.
concept.intuition: An A-trade is the one you trained for - your best pattern, in the right market, at the right time; that is where size belongs.
concept.mechanics: Setups are graded before entry against confluence criteria (pattern quality, trend, volume, catalyst, time of day, recent tracked performance of the setup); A grades receive maximum planned risk, lower grades reduced or zero size. Grades are audited in daily review against outcomes per grade.
concept.failure_modes: Grade inflation under overconfidence or FOMO turns marginal trades into 'A-trades'; without per-grade outcome tracking the label is decoration. Even genuine A-setups lose often - the grade governs size, not the result.
concept.misconceptions: An A-trade is not a guaranteed winner; it is a bet-sizing category grounded in historical expectancy of the pattern class. Confidence felt in the moment is not a grading criterion.
concept.example: Earnings-gap momentum continuation with triple relative volume in a trending tape grades A and takes the full 1R risk; the same pattern pre-market in thin volume does not.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
